source.title: A Survey on Physics Informed Reinforcement Learning: Review and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: How can physics-informed reinforcement learning learn compressed, informative, and physically relevant latent representations from high-dimensional continuous state or action spaces? In this context, physics-informed reinforcement learning means incorporating physics structures, priors, or real-world physical variables into reinforcement-learning policy learning or optimization, and the desired representations should use or be guided by underlying physics during representation learning or feature extraction so that the resulting features remain both informative for the learning task and physically pertinent.

evidence.quote: The concept of physics-informed RL involves incorporating physics structures, priors, and real-world physical variables into the policy learning or optimization process.

But learning a compressed and informative latent space from high dimensional continuous state (or action) space still remains a hurdle. Also learning physically relevant representation is still an open problem. Future research should address this issue and try to devise approaches that helps to incorporate or take guidance of underlying physics during representation learning or feature extraction, so as to make them both informative and physically pertinent.

accepted.question_text: How can physics-informed reinforcement learning provide model-agnostic safe exploration and control for reinforcement-learning agents operating in complex and uncertain environments? The question asks for methods that do not depend on a specific approximated system model or a pre-specified safe-state set, while still enabling the agent to respect safety constraints during exploration and learned-policy deployment.

evidence.quote: Safe reinforcement learning involves learning control policies that guarantee system performance and respect safety constraints during both exploration and policy deployment.

But these approaches are limited by the approximated model of the system and the prior knowledge about safe state sets. There has been a lot of research for better system identification or model learning through physics incorporation. But most works do not generalize well to different tasks and environments. To summarize, future works should address these crucial research goals: 1) model agnostic safe exploration and control using RL agents in complex and uncertain environments and 2) devise generalized approach of incorporating physics in data-driven Model learning.

accepted.question_text: How can physics be incorporated in data-driven model learning in a way that generalizes across different tasks and environments in physics-informed reinforcement learning? The problem is to devise a generalized approach for using physics information when learning or improving environment or system models, rather than methods that work only for one task or one environment.

evidence.quote: The concept of physics-informed RL involves incorporating physics structures, priors, and real-world physical variables into the policy learning or optimization process.

There has been a lot of research for better system identification or model learning through physics incorporation. But most works do not generalize well to different tasks and environments. To summarize, future works should address these crucial research goals: 1) model agnostic safe exploration and control using RL agents in complex and uncertain environments and 2) devise generalized approach of incorporating physics in data-driven Model learning.

accepted.question_text: How can researchers choose and organize physics priors for physics-informed reinforcement learning through a comprehensive framework that can handle novel physical tasks? The framework should account for the fact that useful physics priors can vary from one case to another even within the same domain, and should reduce the need to design each physics-informed reinforcement-learning task individually.

evidence.quote: Depending on the specific problem or scenario, different physics priors can be integrated using various RL methods at different stages of the RL framework, see Fig. 4.

Choice of the physics prior is very crucial for the PIRL algorithm. But such choice is difficult and requires extensive study of the system and may vary extensively from one case to another even in same domains. To enhance efficacy, devising a comprehensive framework with physics information to manage novel physical tasks is preferable rather than dealing with tasks individually.

accepted.question_text: How can the physics-informed reinforcement learning community build comprehensive benchmarking and evaluation environments that allow new physics-informed approaches and algorithms to be tested, compared fairly, and assessed for quality and uniqueness across diverse application domains? The benchmark should address the current dependence on customized, domain-specific environments and the need for domain expertise to understand and compare physics-information choices.

evidence.quote: Currently, PIRL doesn’t have comprehensive benchmarking and evaluation environments to test and compare new physics approaches before induction. This limitation makes it challenging to assess the quality and uniqueness of new works.

Additionally, most PIRL works rely on customized environments related to a particular domain, making it difficult to compare PIRL algorithms fairly. Moreover, PIRL application cases are diverse, and the physics information chosen is specific to a domain, requiring extensive study and domain expertise to understand and compare such works.
